title: pinmux: pad sleep behavior enable after reset
conditions: Immediately after the pinmux register reset, before software writes MIO_PAD_SLEEP_EN or DIO_PAD_SLEEP_EN.
"Drive" means that the pad keeps being driven by its normal source on sleep entry, i.e. no sleep behavior (tie-low, tie-high, high-Z or keep) is applied; this corresponds to sleep enable 0.

requirements.note: First row of the sleep behavior table (heading at line 64): sleep enable 0, any sleep mode, behavior Drive, marked as the default. The table covers both MIO (`mio_pad_sleep_en`) and DIO (`dio_pad_sleep_en`) pads.

requirements.text: Note that if the behavior is set to "Drive", the sleep mode will not be activated upon sleep entry.

design.note: Reset value of the EN field of the MIO_PAD_SLEEP_EN multireg. Source for every top.

The sleep status of an MIO pad is set on sleep entry only if its sleep enable is 1 (line 519); with enable 0 the pad keeps its normal output (lines 495 to 501).
The same gating for DIO pads (line 555).

generated_from_same_input: The register flops in each top's pinmux_reg_top.sv (D2, D3, D5, D6) and the reset values in registers.md are generated by reggen from the same pinmux.hjson, rendered from the template (D1, D4), so their agreement is not independent evidence. The programmers' guide (R1, R2) is written by hand and is the independent requirement.
finding: The guide marks Drive (sleep enable 0) as the default sleep behavior. The design agrees: every MIO and DIO sleep enable resets to 0 in both tops checked, and with enable 0 the pad's sleep status is never set on sleep entry.
ambiguities: MIO_PAD_SLEEP_MODE resets to 2 (high-Z), which the table lists as the High-Z behavior for sleep enable 1. A reader could take the mode's reset value for the default behavior; the table's "-" in the first row makes clear that the mode is ignored while the enable is 0.
observations_outside_this_case: Line 61 of the same guide has a malformed link, "via the (registers.md#mio_pad_sleep_en)", with the link text missing.
out_of_scope: Behavior on sleep entry and exit, which depends on the power manager's sleep request; a simulation would be needed to observe it.
purpose: Control case: a statement that agrees with the design, used to measure false alarms when later checks are evaluated on these cases.
